setup: Stand tall, bar resting on your thighs
Elbows by your sides, wrists straight
execution: Curl the bar up, knuckles leading
Keep your wrists in line with forearms
Lower slowly all the way down
faults: Don't swing your hips to lift it
Don't let your wrists drop back
Don't let your elbows drift behind you

notes: Use noticeably less weight than your normal curl; the overhand grip is weaker.
An EZ bar's angled grip can be easier on the wrists than a straight bar.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Hammer curl
regressions.reason: Neutral grip; stronger and easier on the wrists.

progressions.name: Reverse curl with slow lowering
progressions.reason: A 3-second lowering adds work without more weight.

substitutions.name: Hammer curl
substitutions.reason: Also targets the forearm and brachialis; load is each dumbbell.

substitutions.name: Cable reverse curl
substitutions.reason: Same grip on a cable with a straight bar; stack load.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at elbow height, figure facing right. The overhand grip (knuckles up, facing forward at the top) must be clear.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall, arms straight, bar resting against the thighs with an overhand grip, knuckles facing forward. Elbows by the sides, wrists straight.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Elbows bent so the bar is near the front of the shoulders, knuckles facing up and forward. Upper arms still by the sides, wrists in line with the forearms.

guideBrief.barPath: An arc from the thighs up to the front of the shoulders
